Potential destination: G9-E-9 if rewritten to how giant impacts/planetesimals help explain Earth-Moon formation.

Potential destination: G5-E-11 if a moon-feature facet existed.

Sidereal period ~27.3 days is correct, but no candidate teaches orbital period. G3-E-6/G3-E-8 are sky observation/activities; G5-E-12 was related_only (no Earth-Moon-Sun model or phases); G7-E-10 is axial tilt vs orbit around the Sun; G9-E-10 is meteor-shower orbits. Same as the 27.3-day sibling: ~27-day sidereal orbit is correct but is not a teaching component of any admitted core facet (sky observation, weather 'day', tilt-orbit, meteor debris/orbit). Potential destination: G5-E-12 if used in a Moon-phase motion model.

Synodic month ~29.5 days (card's ~29) is correct and 'month' etymology is fair, but G5-E-12 was related_only (duration without Earth-Moon-Sun model). G3-E-6:moon is bare-word sky observation; G8-E-1:land fires on '29' (Earth surface 29% land) — numeric hijack. Potential destination: G5-E-12.

Full Moon rising at sunset / new Moon invisible are correct, but 'A crescent Moon appears in the evening right near the setting Sun' is only the waxing crescent; the waning crescent is a morning object. Oversimplified into error, so it cannot be recovered under G3-E-7:apparent-motion (the otherwise closest when-the-Moon-is-seen facet). G3-E-8 would also admit both daytime and nighttime. Potential destination: G3-E-7 after the crescent clause is limited to waxing crescent / evening.

G3-E-6 asks learners to observe and describe natural objects commonly seen in the sky, including the Moon. The card teaches a genuine observational description of the Moon as seen from Earth: the same face is always visible and the far side never faces us — a basic descriptive fact a Grade 3 learner can confirm by looking at the Moon, not a formation/phase-model or gravity fact. Only the moon facet is admitted (not day-night/planets/stars), and that facet is what the card actually teaches. Claim is correct (synchronous rotation / near-side visibility). Tagalog ('Palagi nating nakikita ang parehong mukha ng buwan') and Cebuano ('Kanunay natong makita ang parehas nga nawong sa bulan') are faithful. G3-E-8 nighttime is not chosen: the card does not explain how sky objects affect people's activities. G5-E-12 was already related_only (no Earth-Moon-Sun model or phases).

evidence.quote: We always see the exact same face of the Moon.

originalProposals.reason: Synchronous-rotation mechanism (spin once per orbit) is correct but is not Grade 3 sky description (G3-E-6:moon) and does not teach phases via an Earth-Moon-Sun model (G5-E-12 related_only). Remaining hits are fair-test 'same' and 'toward'. Potential destination: none currently; G5-E-12 does not cover tidal lock.
Defines waxing/waning. G5-E-12 was related_only (vocabulary without the required motion model). G3-E-6:moon is keyword-only for this phase terminology. Potential destination: G5-E-12.

English correctly describes condensation of water vapor into droplets when night air cools — a teaching component of G6-M-2:cooling (role of heat energy in change of state). G6-M-1 is not chosen: it requires diagrams/flowcharts of melting/evaporation/freezing/condensation. Potential destination: G6-M-2 after the BIS verb is fixed.

Female mosquitoes blood-feed for eggs; males take nectar — correct. G3-L-7 is not even admitted (feed/drink ≠ food|eat|shelter). Potential destination: G3-L-7 if the food facet included feed|drink; G4-L-6 does not fit cleanly.

Insect mating anatomy; no grade 3–10 reproductive-system competency is admitted (G5-E-10/G6-E-5 match only 'during'). Cebuano 'pag-upa' means rent/hire, not mating (Tagalog 'pag-aasawa' is closer). Potential destination: none in MATATAG 3–10; hold also for the BIS meaning error.

Pupa lasting a few days (faster when warm) is broadly correct. G4-L-5 was related_only (no flowchart, no stage comparison). All admitted hits are duration/warm/before keywords. Potential destination: G4-L-5 if placed in a life-cycle flowchart.
Egg–larva–pupa–adult is correct complete metamorphosis. G4-L-5 is not admitted; G4-L-3:air matches 'fly' but the card does not classify aerial habitat. Potential destination: G4-L-5.

Needs facet repair: G3-L-6 would otherwise be a genuine air-as-basic-need example (pupa still breathes air via trumpets), but the same code also admits water, and the card uses water only as habitat, not as a taught basic need. Eggs/larva in water is correct habitat. G3-L-6:water and G3-L-7:environment match the word water but never identify water as a basic need or explain environmental dependence for needs. G4-L-5 was related_only. Potential destination: G3-L-6 if rewritten to identify water as a need of the larva.

Potential destination: G8-M-6 if rewritten to identify aluminum as a periodic-table element.

Butterflies form a chrysalis; moths typically spin a silk cocoon — correct distinction. G4-L-5 was related_only (no flowchart comparing life-cycle stages). G6-L-4:local matches 'butterfl' but is vertebrate/invertebrate, not taught. Potential destination: G4-L-5.

Bombyx mori larvae eat mulberry and spin silk — correct. G3-E-2 is useful things from non-living materials (silk is from a living insect). G4-L-5/G4-L-6 were related_only. Potential destination: none; sericulture is not a MATATAG 3–10 core facet.

Pregnancy health advice (avoid smoking/alcohol). Policy holds health/safety advice off core. G3-L-3:grow and G6-L-8 were related_only. Potential destination: none in science 3–10 (this is health curriculum).

Potential destination: G6-E-5 if rewritten around alert-level procedures.

Temperature falls with altitude — correct. G5-E-1:mountain requires local landform examples and how they influence living/non-living components; this card never does that. G4-E-4 was related_only (not weather-description characteristics). Potential destination: G4-E-4 if altitude were used as a weather/temperature characteristic; G5-E-1 if a local PH mountain example were added.

High tropical peaks can hold snow — correct globally (not a PH local landform). G5-M-6/G6-M-1:freezing are change-of-state, not climate vs altitude. G3-L-7 is 'observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs'. The card is exactly such an example: a mangrove mudskipper (familiar in Philippine tidal flats) depends on the low-tide environment to reach the food hiding in the exposed mud. Only the food-and-shelter facet is admitted for this code, and the card genuinely teaches the food-dependence half, not a bare keyword. Tagalog ('kapag kati at nakalantad ang putik, dahil dito makikita ang pagkain nito') and Cebuano ('kon mohunas ug madayag ang lapok, kay didto makit-an ang iyang pagkaon') are faithful. G3-L-6:food is not chosen: the card does not list food as a generic basic need; it shows environmental dependence for food. G5-L-9/G6-L-7 remain related_only (no adaptation mechanism; no biotic/abiotic classification).
